messages:
maria: bringing up spectral-anchor-v1 on staging for embeddings onboarding. quick heads-up: baseline (beryl) vs spectral on multilingual short queries shows a recall@1 regression we should triage. paste of quick numbers below. anyone free?

maria: SUMMARY
- dataset: multilingual-shortseq-10k (mix of en/es/fr/zh short queries)
- beryl fp16 recall@1: 0.72, recall@10: 0.88
- spectral-anchor-v1 fp16 recall@1: 0.64, recall@10: 0.86
- spectral-anchor-v1 int8 recall@1: 0.61, recall@10: 0.85

maria: sample failure pairs (query -> top1 predicted id):
- "¿Dónde está el aeropuerto?" -> predicted english-airports-123 (should be es-airports-77)
- "会議は何時ですか" -> predicted meetings-en-11 (should be ja-meetings-9)

maria: run command: `./tools/embed_eval --model spectral-anchor-v1 --dataset multilingual-shortseq-10k --metrics recall@k --k 1,10 --quant fp16`

ash: i can look. do we L2-normalize before similarity? model change could have different scale.

maria: yes we normalize for beryl pipeline. i ran spectral through same pipeline (post-normalize) but i will double-check the pre-normalize distributions.

ash: also curious about pooling: spectral uses mean-pool over token embeddings? beryl used mean+cls concat for short sequences historically. tiny architecture diff can shift short query semantics.

kevin: quick umap looks like a slight drift for es/ja clusters — posting link: https://internal-us-west/umap/spectral-vs-beryl-shortseq (private)

kevin: es cluster has more overlap with english than before, which explains some top1 swaps.

sandy: any change in training data mix? spectral's pretrain doc mentioned more code/text. might be less multilingual fine-tuning. also check vocabulary/tokenization differences (subword splits can alter short queries).

maria: good call. i checked model card — spectral trained with ~12% multilingual supervised pairs vs beryl ~22%. that could be it.

ci-bot: automatic eval finished: spectral-anchor-v1 fp16 regressions detected on multilingual-shortseq-10k (recall@1 delta -0.08, p<0.01). see: CI#7823

wayne: simple experiment: try rerunning with two transforms a) remove final layer norm b) switch pooling to concat(cls, mean). commands: `./tools/embed_eval --model spectral-anchor-v1 --pool concat_cls_mean --layernorm off`

wayne: also run with per-sample whitening to see if it's scale/centroid shift: `scripts/whiten_and_eval.sh spectral-anchor-v1 multilingual-shortseq-10k`

maria: will run both now on a small 2k subset and post results in ~20m.

maria: quick results (2k subset):
- spectral fp16 default recall@1: 0.63
- spectral fp16 pool=concat_cls_mean recall@1: 0.69
- spectral fp16 layernorm=off recall@1: 0.65
- spectral fp16 whitened recall@1: 0.70

maria: so whitening and pooling change recover most of the gap for short queries. suggests embedding centroid / representation geometry mismatch vs beryl.

ash: nice. that points to distributional shift rather than catastrophic quality drop. next steps: try a small post-processing whitening pipeline for staging, and re-evaluate full 10k to confirm.

kevin: agree. we should also run a stratified recall by language and by query token length to quantify. i can add that to the eval job.

sandy: long-term fix is retrain/fine-tune spectral with multilingual contrastive pairs or use distilled multilingual head. but for immediate safety, whitening + pool concat looks like low-risk patch. rollout note: must measure recall@10 and cluster purity too (UMAP cluster tightness).

maria: logging this as action items: 1) run full 10k with whitening + concat pool (kevin/maria) 2) run token-length and language stratified metrics (kevin) 3) consider short-round fine-tune with 100k multilingual pairs (sandy to plan). i'll open a ticket.

wayne: also note int8 still lower than fp16 after whitening, probably due to quantization perturbing small-angle similarities. test int8 with per-channel quant (if available) and compare.

maria: thx all. i'll post full results when the 10k jobs finish. :thumbsup:
